title: Behavioural interview questions (sample)
description: Core behavioural prompts with guidance, answer frameworks and self-review checklists. They contain no personal answers.

behaviouralQuestions.title: Tell me about yourself
guidance: Give a short, structured story rather than reciting your CV: where you are now, how you got here, and where you are heading.
Aim for 60 to 90 seconds. End by connecting your path to investment banking and to this conversation.

steps.label: Present
steps.hint: What you are doing now (course, role) and one headline strength or result.

steps.label: Past
steps.hint: Two or three experiences that built your skills and led you to finance, in order.

steps.label: Future
steps.hint: Why investment banking next, and what you want to contribute.

checklist: Under 90 seconds
Has a clear beginning, middle and end
Mentions one or two specific achievements
Ends by linking to investment banking
Sounds like me, not a script

behaviouralQuestions.title: Why investment banking?
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Why do you want to work in investment banking?
guidance: Interviewers look for a reason that is specific, evidenced and honest. Avoid generic answers about money or prestige.
Show you understand the job: long hours, learning curve, client work. Then say why that appeals to you.

steps.label: Interest
steps.hint: What draws you to the work itself: deals, valuation, advising companies.

steps.label: Evidence
steps.hint: What you have done to test that interest: courses, deals followed, internships, competitions.

steps.label: Fit
steps.hint: Why your skills and temperament suit the role and the training.

checklist: Gives a reason beyond pay and prestige
Backs the interest with something I have actually done
Shows I understand what the job involves
Mentions at least one specific deal or sector
Stays under 90 seconds

behaviouralQuestions.title: Why this firm?
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Why do you want to work at this firm in particular?
guidance: Make it specific to the firm: its sectors, recent deals, culture and the people you spoke to. Replace the placeholder firm name when you write your answer.
Create your own copy of this question for each firm you are interviewing with, so each answer is saved separately.

steps.label: Firm
steps.hint: One or two things the firm is known for that matter to you, such as a sector or deal.

steps.label: People
steps.hint: Who you spoke to or what you learned from events or alumni.

steps.label: Me
steps.hint: How your background and goals line up with what the firm does.

checklist: Names something only this firm could be described by
Mentions a recent deal, team or conversation
Does not repeat my answer for another firm
Links back to my own background
Under 90 seconds

behaviouralQuestions.title: Tell me about a time you led a team
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Tell me about a time you showed leadership.
guidance: Leadership does not need a title. Choose an example where you set direction, organised others or took ownership when it was unclear who would.
Be clear about your own role, then show how you brought others with you.

steps.label: Situation
steps.hint: Set the scene briefly: the team, the goal, why it needed leading.

steps.label: Task
steps.hint: What you were responsible for and the challenge.

steps.label: Action
steps.hint: The specific steps you took to organise, motivate or decide.

steps.label: Result
steps.hint: The outcome, with numbers if you can, and what the team or you learned.

checklist: Opens with a specific situation, not a general statement
Says what I personally was responsible for
Describes what I did (I), not only what the team did (we)
Gives a concrete result, with numbers where possible
Says what I learned or would do differently
Fits in about two minutes

behaviouralQuestions.title: Tell me about a time you worked in a team
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked effectively in a team.
guidance: Pick a team situation with a real difficulty (tight deadline, uneven workload) rather than a smooth one.
Show what you contributed and how you supported others.

steps.label: Situation
steps.hint: The team, the project and the pressure it was under.

steps.label: Task
steps.hint: Your part and what the team needed from you.

steps.label: Action
steps.hint: What you did to contribute, coordinate or help a teammate.

steps.label: Result
steps.hint: The result for the project and how the team worked afterwards.

checklist: Opens with a specific situation, not a general statement
Says what I personally was responsible for
Describes what I did (I), not only what the team did (we)
Gives a concrete result, with numbers where possible
Says what I learned or would do differently
Fits in about two minutes

behaviouralQuestions.title: Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had a conflict or disagreement with a colleague or teammate, and how you handled it.
guidance: Choose a real but professional disagreement. Focus on how you listened, found the underlying issue and reached an outcome.
Avoid blaming the other person; show maturity and respect.

steps.label: Situation
steps.hint: Who disagreed and about what, in one or two sentences.

steps.label: Task
steps.hint: What was at stake for you and the team.

steps.label: Action
steps.hint: How you raised it, listened and worked toward agreement.

steps.label: Result
steps.hint: How it ended and what you do differently now.

checklist: Opens with a specific situation, not a general statement
Says what I personally was responsible for
Describes what I did (I), not only what the team did (we)
Gives a concrete result, with numbers where possible
Says what I learned or would do differently
Fits in about two minutes

behaviouralQuestions.title: Tell me about a time you failed
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: Tell me about a time you failed or made a significant mistake.
guidance: Choose a genuine mistake with a real consequence, own it plainly and spend most of the answer on what you changed afterwards.
Avoid disguised strengths such as working too hard.

steps.label: Situation
steps.hint: What you were doing and what went wrong.

steps.label: Task
steps.hint: What you were meant to deliver or protect.

steps.label: Action
steps.hint: What you did once you knew, including telling people and fixing it.

steps.label: Result
steps.hint: The outcome and the specific habit or process you changed.

checklist: Opens with a specific situation, not a general statement
Says what I personally was responsible for
Describes what I did (I), not only what the team did (we)
Gives a concrete result, with numbers where possible
Says what I learned or would do differently
Fits in about two minutes

behaviouralQuestions.title: Strengths and weaknesses
behaviouralQuestions.prompt: What are your greatest strengths and weaknesses?
guidance: Choose one or two strengths that matter in banking, each with a short example. Choose a real weakness that is not essential to the job and show what you are doing about it.

steps.label: Strength
steps.hint: One strength relevant to the role, stated plainly.

steps.label: Evidence
steps.hint: A short example that proves it.

steps.label: Weakness and fix
steps.hint: A real weakness and the concrete step you are taking to improve it.

checklist: Strength is relevant to banking and evidenced
Weakness is real, not a disguised strength
Says what I am doing to improve
Balanced: not all strength or all weakness
Under 90 seconds
